extracted.intended_audience: Authors, editors, and contributors to systematic reviews (Cochrane and non‑Cochrane); methodologists and evidence synthesis practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for planning, conducting, synthesizing, assessing bias in, reporting, and updating systematic reviews of interventions (Cochrane context but applicable more broadly). Emphasis on rigorous methods (meta‑analysis, risk‑of‑bias tools, sources of evidence), planning to handle heterogeneity/multiplicity, and producing reviews useful for decision‑making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cochrane Reviews should answer important, decision‑relevant questions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Cochrane Reviews should answer important questions that are relevant to decision‑making."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects breadth of questions; guidance is supplemented by material on intervention complexity and equity so reviews inform policy, clinical, or consumer decisions. Reviews should be targeted to the needs of decision makers and consider multiple intervention options when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan the review in depth before analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: "New guidance provides in‑depth support for planning the review... Planning ahead will provide more support to authors at the analysis stages of the review and is of particular assistance for reviews with high levels of heterogeneity or multiplicity of outcome measures."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should plan methods (including grouping and synthesis strategies) in advance to handle heterogeneity and multiple outcomes; good planning reduces analytic ambiguity and supports robust synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct good, explicit review questions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulating clear, well‑scoped questions is foundational; explicit methods (what was done and why) should be documented so users can judge applicability and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group included studies by population, intervention, and outcomes for synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: "Grouping included studies according to their populations, interventions, and outcomes for synthesis."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use predefined grouping strategies to organize synthesis and explore heterogeneity; grouping should be planned and justified in methods to support transparent analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address intervention complexity and equity in synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: "Guidance for meta‑analysis is now supplemented by new guidance on intervention complexity and equity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider contextual factors, complexity of interventions, and equity impacts when planning, synthesizing, and interpreting results so findings are relevant across populations and settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and use network meta‑analysis when comparing multiple interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: "A major new chapter addresses network meta‑analysis to support such decisions, and Cochrane is actively encouraging the appropriate use of this methodology."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When decision makers must choose among multiple options, use network meta‑analysis appropriately; authors should follow the Handbook's dedicated chapter for methods, assumptions, and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand and apply guidance on use of non‑randomized studies
rubrics_metrics.description: "The guidance on the use of non‑randomized studies has been extensively expanded."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where randomized evidence is lacking or insufficient, follow the Handbook's expanded methods for identifying, appraising, and synthesizing non‑randomized studies, including appropriate risk‑of‑bias assessment (see ROBINS‑I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use updated meta‑analysis methods and consider alternatives to traditional meta‑analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: "Updated guidance on meta‑analysis and new statistical methods are supplemented by an all‑new chapter on alternatives to traditional meta‑analysis for synthesis of results across studies."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply contemporary statistical methods for meta‑analysis; where traditional pooling is inappropriate, consult alternative synthesis approaches (narrative synthesis, evidence integration techniques) described in the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify evidence sources beyond published trials (e.g., clinical study reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Updated guidance on identifying sources of evidence includes information on sources other than published trials (such as clinical study reports)... an extended technical supplement on sources to search."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search a broad set of sources (gray literature, trial registers, clinical study reports) to reduce publication bias and ensure comprehensive evidence retrieval; follow the Handbook's technical supplement for search strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate technical advances in search and evidence identification (text mining, machine learning) and prospective approaches (living systematic reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: "An introduction to the role of technical advances such as text mining and machine learning, and prospective approaches such as living systematic reviews."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider automated and semi‑automated tools to enhance search efficiency and updating; adopt living review methods where continual evidence accumulation justifies ongoing updating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess risk of bias in randomized trials using RoB 2
rubrics_metrics.description: "...dedicated chapters on the RoB 2 tool for assessing bias in randomized trials..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the RoB 2 framework to evaluate potential bias domains in RCTs; follow the Handbook's chapter for application, signaling questions, and interpretation of RoB 2 outputs in synthesis and GRADE/summary assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess risk of bias in non‑randomized studies using ROBINS‑I
rubrics_metrics.description: "...the ROBINS‑I tool for assessing bias in non‑randomized studies of interventions..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply ROBINS‑I to judge bias in observational intervention studies; integrate ROBINS‑I findings into overall evidence appraisal and consider confounding, selection, measurement, and other bias domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider reporting biases and bias due to missing results in a synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: "...a new framework for considering reporting biases and bias due to missing results in a synthesis."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly assess and report the risk that selective non‑reporting or missing results have biased the synthesis; use the Handbook's framework to identify, evaluate, and mitigate reporting biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refresh and apply core methods that underpin every review
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is also revised guidance on the basics, refreshing those core methods that underpin every review."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to fundamental systematic review methods (clear eligibility criteria, transparent selection, data extraction, synthesis plans) as updated in the Handbook to ensure trustworthy reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document clearly what was done and why; use guidelines but apply judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: "...whatever is done, reviewers should clearly explain what was done, and why" and "these guidelines are not a substitute for good judgement."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, explicit methods and rationales in reviews so users can assess validity and applicability; apply professional judgement—guidance informs but does not replace thoughtful methodological decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cochrane‑specific operational guidance: planning, logistics, reporting, and updating
rubrics_metrics.description: "For authors working with Cochrane, new online‑only chapters will provide guidance specific to Cochrane Reviews, covering the planning and logistics stages of Cochrane Reviews as well as guidance on reporting and updating reviews."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cochrane authors should follow the online chapters for operational steps (registration, managing editorial workflow, reporting standards, updating procedures) in addition to general methods guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide training and resources to help contributors meet high standards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Cochrane also provides a range of training and other guidance for authors, editors and other contributors to systematic reviews to assist them in meeting the high standards expected (training.cochrane.org)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and editors are expected to use available training and methodological resources to apply Handbook guidance appropriately; capacity building supports quality and consistency across reviews.
